canonical_question: Which specific elements (W, Mo, Ta) were replaced by which lighter elements (Ti, Hf, Zr) to obtain HfNbTaTiZr, and was the molar ratio preserved?

question_variants.question: Which specific elements (W, Mo, Ta) were replaced by which lighter elements (Ti, Hf, Zr) to obtain HfNbTaTiZr, and was the molar ratio preserved?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The cited work by Senkov et al. replaced heavy elements W, Mo, and Ta with lighter elements Ti, Hf, and Zr to obtain HfNbTaTiZr. The provided evidence confirms the replacement of these specific elements but does not explicitly state if the molar ratios were preserved in the replacement process.

answers.answer: Senkov et al. [18] explored the possibility of replacing heavy elements W, Mo and Ta with lighter elements Ti, Hf and Zr and successfully obtained HfNbTaTiZr RHEAs. The text confirms the specific elements replaced but does not specify if molar ratios were preserved.
answers.mechanism: Replacement of heavy elements with lighter elements
answers.boundary_limitation: Molar ratio preservation not specified in evidence
evidence_spans: Thus, Senkov et al. [18] explored the possibility of replacing heavy elements W, Mo and Ta with lighter elements Ti, Hf and Zr and successfully obtained HfNbTaTiZr RHEAs, which also have a BCC crystal structure. HfNbTaTiZr possesses outstanding room temperature ductility ( ε > 50%) and considerable strain hardening and its yield strength reaches 929 MPa. Intriguingly, its yield strength at elevated temperature (1000 °C) is poor, which is only 295 MPa.
